504	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
505	
506	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
507	
508	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
509	
510	### How connector nodes reference bindings
511	
512	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
513	
514	```json
515	"context": [
516	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
517	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
518	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
519	]
520	```
521	
522	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
523	
524	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
525	
526	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)
527	
528	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. The schema below is the shape the CLI emits, for **inspection** when debugging a flow's binding state and as the planned shape for the **No-Live-Tenant** flow's sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` (see § No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration above). Per the [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) rules, `bindings[]` is part of the CLI-owned envelope for connector / connector-trigger / managed HTTP nodes.
529	
530	For every unique connection used in the flow, `node configure` appends **two entries** to top-level `bindings[]`:
531	
532	```json
533	"bindings": [
534	  {
535	    "id": "<CONN_BINDING_ID>",
536	    "name": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
537	    "type": "string",
538	    "resource": "Connection",
539	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
540	    "default": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
541	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
542	  },
543	  {
544	    "id": "<FOLDER_BINDING_ID>",
545	    "name": "FolderKey",
546	    "type": "string",
547	    "resource": "Connection",
548	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
549	    "default": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
550	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
551	  }
552	]
553	```
554	
555	| Field | Value |
556	|-------|-------|
557	| `id` | Unique string within the file. Descriptive (e.g. `bJiraConn`) or short random (e.g. `bKEFLMRB2`). |
558	| `name` (connection binding) | The IS connection name (e.g. `"chandu.lella@uipath.com #3"`). `uip maestro flow node configure` fetches this from IS automatically — this is the supported path. The placeholder form `"<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"` appears in the table for reference only (e.g. when inspecting a flow whose bindings have not yet been configured); it must match the definition's `model.context[].connection` placeholder (without the `<bindings.` prefix and `>` suffix). |
559	| `name` (folder binding) | Literal `"FolderKey"` — matches `<bindings.FolderKey>`. |
560	| `type` | Always `"string"`. |
561	| `resource` | Always `"Connection"` — capital C, case-sensitive. |
562	| `resourceKey` | The connection UUID from `uip is connections list`. **Same UUID on both bindings.** |
563	| `default` | Connection binding → connection UUID. Folder binding → folder key. |
564	| `propertyAttribute` | `"ConnectionId"` or `"FolderKey"` — case matters. |
565	
566	The connector node instance carries no `model` block and no binding/context data. `uip maestro flow node configure` populates only `inputs.detail` on the instance and appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries. The connection UUID is held on the binding entry (`resourceKey`), not on the node.
567	
568	> **CLI side-effect — duplicate empty bindings.** `node configure` currently appends placeholder entries with `resourceKey: ""` and no `default` alongside the resolved pair (4 entries per configure call instead of 2). Validate passes; they're harmless but verbose. Remove the empty pair via `Edit` after configure if you care about clean diffs.
569	
570	**Share bindings across nodes using the same connection.** If two connector nodes share the same `<CONNECTION_UUID>`, reuse the same two binding entries — do not add duplicates. Matching is by `name` only (the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder is unique per connector), so any node whose definition resolves against `<bindings.<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection>` picks up the shared binding pair.
571	
572	### Single-connector example (Jira)
573

575	"bindings": [
576	  {
577	    "id": "bJiraConn",
578	    "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",
579	    "type": "string",
580	    "resource": "Connection",
581	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
582	    "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
583	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
584	  },
585	  {
586	    "id": "bJiraFolder",
587	    "name": "FolderKey",
588	    "type": "string",
589	    "resource": "Connection",
590	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
591	    "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
592	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
593	  }
594	]
595	```

598	
599	Two unique connections → four entries in `bindings[]` (two per connection):
600	
601	```json
602	"bindings": [
603	  { "id": "bJiraConn",   "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",   "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
604	  { "id": "bJiraFolder", "name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "folder-uuid-for-jira",                "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" },
605	  { "id": "bSlackConn",  "name": "uipath-salesforce-slack connection", "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
606	  { "id": "bSlackFolder","name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "folder-uuid-for-slack",               "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" }
607	]

610	Both `FolderKey` entries share the same `name` but have distinct `resourceKey`s — that's how the runtime keeps them separate.
611	
612	### Generated `bindings_v2.json` (reference only — do not edit)
613	
614	At debug/pack time, the CLI derives `content/bindings_v2.json` from the top-level `bindings[]` above. One `Connection` resource per unique `resourceKey`; the `FolderKey` bindings are absorbed as metadata (they do not produce standalone resource entries). The generated output looks like:
615	
616	```json
617	{
618	  "version": "2.0",
619	  "resources": [
620	    {
621	      "resource": "Connection",
622	      "key": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
623	      "id": "Connection7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
624	      "value": {
625	        "ConnectionId": {
626	          "defaultValue": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
627	          "isExpression": false,
628	          "displayName": "my-jira-connection"
629	        }
630	      },
631	      "metadata": {
632	        "ActivityName": "Create Issue",
633	        "BindingsVersion": "2.2",
634	        "DisplayLabel": "my-jira-connection",
635	        "UseConnectionService": "true",

637	      }
638	    }
639	  ]
640	}
641	```
642	
643	- `id` is always `"Connection" + <resourceKey>` (concatenated, no separator) — generated, not authored.
644	- `metadata.Connector` is derived from the definition's `model.context[].connectorKey`.
645	- `metadata.ActivityName` comes from the matched node's `display.label`.
646

648	
649	For connector-trigger flows, the same pattern applies — top-level `bindings[]` entries with additional metadata; the CLI derives `EventTrigger` and `Property` resources for `bindings_v2.json`. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md) for the trigger-specific shape.

654	| `EventTrigger` | Top-level `bindings[]` + the trigger node itself | See connector-trigger plugin |
655	| `Property` | Trigger node's `model.inputs.filterFields` | See connector-trigger plugin |

Compare the emitted shape against the CLI-emitted reference in § Top-level `bindings[]` shape. |

The runtime side works but Studio Web has no tree to render. | Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` with `--detail '{"filter": {...tree...}}'` — the CLI populates both halves. Studio Web emits its `Map<string,string\|null>` as `Array.from(entries())` — tuples, not object | Convert to tuples: `[["key", "value"], ...]`. See Step 6c. |

CLI does not validate token coverage. |
682	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails has unknown keys: ObjectActionName, ParameterValues` | PascalCase inner keys instead of camelCase | Use `objectActionName` / `parameterValues`. Studio Web emits camelCase; PascalCase is rejected. |

685	### Debug Tips
686	
687	1. **Always check top-level `bindings[]` in the `.flow` file** — connector nodes silently fail if a binding is missing or malformed. Compare against the CLI-emitted `bindings[]` shape documented above (§ Top-level `bindings[]` shape). Do not inspect `bindings_v2.json` as ground truth; it is regenerated from the `.flow` on every debug/pack.
688	2. **Compare inputs against metadataFile** — the full metadata (from `is resources describe`) has every field with types, descriptions, and whether it's required
689	3. **`flow validate` does NOT catch connector-specific issues** — validation only checks JSON schema and graph structure. Missing `inputs.detail` fields, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime (`flow debug`)
690	4. **If a connector key doesn't work** — list all connectors: `uip is connectors list --output json`. Keys are often prefixed with `uipath-`

692	6. **`node configure` populates bindings automatically** — it appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries and populates `inputs.detail`. The generated `bindings_v2.json` follows from these at debug/pack time. If you cannot run `node configure` (no live tenant, sandbox forbids it, planning-only request), record the planned binding entries in the sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` per the No-Live-Tenant flow above — do not author `bindings[]` directly on the `.flow` as a substitute, and note that the flow will not pass `flow validate` until a real `node configure` runs.

1	# Decision Node — Planning
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.decision`
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	Use a Decision node for binary branching (if/else) based on a boolean condition.
10	
11	### Selection Heuristics
12	
13	| Situation | Use Decision? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Two-path branch based on a boolean condition | Yes |
16	| Three or more paths | No — use [Switch](../switch/planning.md) |
17	| Branch on HTTP response status codes | No — use [HTTP](../http/planning.md) built-in branches |
18	| Branch requires reasoning on ambiguous input | No — use [Agent](../agent/planning.md) |
19	
20	## Ports
21	
22	| Input Port | Output Port(s) |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `input` | `true`, `false` |
25	
26	## Key Inputs
27	
28	| Input | Required | Description |
29	| --- | --- | --- |
30	| `expression` | Yes | Boolean JavaScript expression (e.g., `$vars.fetchData.output.statusCode === 200`) |
31	| `trueLabel` | No | Custom label for the true branch |
32	| `falseLabel` | No | Custom label for the false branch |
33	
34	## Wiring Rules
35	
36	- Decision nodes produce exactly **two** outgoing edges: one from `true`, one from `false`
37	- Both branches must lead to a downstream node (no dangling branches)
38	- Each branch typically ends at its own End node or merges back into a shared path
39

1	# Loop Node — Planning
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.loop`
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	Use a Loop node to iterate over a collection of items. Supports sequential and parallel execution.
10	
11	### Selection Heuristics
12	
13	| Situation | Use Loop? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Process each item in an array | Yes |
16	| Run the same operation on multiple inputs concurrently | Yes (with `parallel: true`) |
17	| Simple data transformation on a collection | No — use [Transform](../transform/planning.md) |
18	| Distribute work items to robots | No — use [Queue](../queue/planning.md) |
19	
20	## Ports
21	
22	| Input Port(s) | Output Port(s) |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `input`, `loopBack` | `success`, `output`, `error` |
25	
26	- `loopBack` — receives the edge returning from the last node inside the loop body
27	- `success` — fires after all iterations complete
28	- `output` — carries aggregated results from all iterations
29	- `error` — implicit error port shared with all action nodes; fires when the loop or an iteration throws. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
30	
31	## Key Inputs
32	
33	| Input | Required | Description |
34	| --- | --- | --- |
35	| `collection` | Yes | Expression pointing to an array (e.g., `$vars.fetchData.output.body.items`) |
36	| `parallel` | No | `true` to execute all iterations concurrently (default: sequential) |
37	
38	## Loop Variables (available inside loop body only)
39	
40	- `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` — the item being processed in this iteration
41	- `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` — 0-based iteration index
42	- `$vars.<loopId>.collection` — the full collection
43	
44	Where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
45	
46	## Wiring Rules
47	
48	- The loop body starts from the `output` port of the loop node
49	- The last node in the loop body connects back to the loop's `loopBack` port
50	- After all iterations, execution continues from the `success` port
51	- Do not create cycles except through the `loopBack` mechanism
52	- **Every node inside the loop body must have `"parentId": "<loopId>"`** — without this, variableUpdates will not fire per-iteration and loop variables will be inaccessible
53

1	# Loop Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.loop`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.loop --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input ports `input` and `loopBack`, output ports `success` and `output`, required input `collection`. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	### Loop node
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "id": "loop1",
22	  "type": "core.logic.loop",
23	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
24	  "display": { "label": "Loop over items" },
25	  "inputs": {
26	    "collection": "=js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items",
27	    "parallel": false
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	Set `"parallel": true` to execute all iterations concurrently.
33	
34	### Loop body nodes — `parentId` required
35	
36	Every node inside the loop body **must** have `"parentId"` set to the loop node's ID. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is part of the loop and variableUpdates will not fire per-iteration.
37	
38	```json
39	{
40	  "id": "processItem",
41	  "type": "core.action.script",
42	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
43	  "display": { "label": "Process item" },
44	  "inputs": {
45	    "script": "return $vars.product * $vars.loop1.currentItem"
46	  },
47	  "parentId": "loop1"
48	}
49	```
50	
51	> **Critical:** If you omit `parentId`, the node executes outside the loop context. State variables will not update across iterations and loop outputs like `currentItem` will be inaccessible.
52	
53	## Adding / Editing
54	
55	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs` and `parentId`.
56	
57	## Wiring
58	
59	Loop nodes have a specific wiring pattern:
60	
61	- `input` — entry from upstream
62	- `output` — into the loop body (first body node)
63	- `loopBack` — return from last body node back to loop
64	- `success` — exit after loop completes (to next downstream node)
65	
66	See [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md) for edge add procedures.
67	
68	## Accessing Loop Variables Inside Body
69	
70	Inside the loop body, access the current item via `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`:
71	
72	```javascript
73	// In a Script node inside the loop body (parentId must be set to the loop node)
74	const item = $vars.loop1.currentItem;
75	const index = $vars.loop1.currentIndex;
76	return { processed: item.name.toUpperCase(), position: index };
77	```
78	
79	| Variable | Description |
80	| --- | --- |
81	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | The item being processed in this iteration |
82	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` | 0-based iteration index |
83	| `$vars.<loopId>.collection` | The full collection being iterated |
84	
85	> **Do not use `iterator.currentItem`.** The correct access pattern is `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
86	
87	### Required node variables for loop outputs
88	
89	For `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` etc. to resolve, you must add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`:
90	
91	```json
92	{
93	  "variables": {
94	    "nodes": [
95	      {
96	        "id": "loop1.currentItem",
97	        "type": "any",
98	        "description": "The current item being iterated in the loop",
99	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" }
100	      },
101	      {
102	        "id": "loop1.currentIndex",
103	        "type": "number",
104	        "description": "The current iteration index (0-based)",
105	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" }
106	      },
107	      {
108	        "id": "loop1.collection",
109	        "type": "array",
110	        "description": "The collection being iterated over",
111	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" }
112	      },
113	      {
114	        "id": "loop1.output",
115	        "type": "array",
116	        "description": "Aggregated results from all loop iterations",
117	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" }
118	      }
119	    ]
120	  }
121	}
122	```
123	
124	## State Accumulation with variableUpdates
125	
126	To accumulate state across loop iterations (counters, running totals), use an `inout` variable with a `variableUpdate` on the body node:
127	
128	```json
129	{
130	  "variables": {
131	    "globals": [
132	      {
133	        "id": "runningTotal",
134	        "direction": "inout",
135	        "type": "number",
136	        "defaultValue": 0
137	      }
138	    ],
139	    "variableUpdates": {
140	      "bodyNode": [
141	        {
142	          "variableId": "runningTotal",
143	          "expression": "=js:$vars.bodyNode.output"
144	        }
145	      ]
146	    }
147	  }
148	}
149	```
150	
151	The variableUpdate fires after each iteration, so the `inout` variable carries the accumulated value into the next iteration.
152	
153	> **Critical:** The variableUpdate expression **cannot** access loop iteration variables like `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`. These are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). If you need to compute using `currentItem`, do the computation in the script and reference the script's output in the variableUpdate.
154	
155	## Complete Example — Loop with State Accumulation
156	
157	A flow that iterates over a collection, accumulates a result in an `inout` variable via a Script body node, and outputs the final value.
158	
159	```json
160	{
161	  "nodes": [
162	    {
163	      "id": "start",
164	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
165	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
166	      "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
167	      "inputs": { "entryPointId": "..." }
168	    },
169	    {
170	      "id": "loop1",
171	      "type": "core.logic.loop",
172	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
173	      "display": { "label": "Loop" },
174	      "inputs": { "collection": "=js:$vars.inputItems", "parallel": false }
175	    },
176	    {
177	      "id": "bodyScript",
178	      "type": "core.action.script",
179	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
180	      "display": { "label": "Process item" },
181	      "inputs": {
182	        "script": "return $vars.accumulator + $vars.loop1.currentItem;"
183	      },
184	      "parentId": "loop1"
185	    },
186	    {
187	      "id": "end1",
188	      "type": "core.control.end",
189	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
190	      "display": { "label": "End" },
191	      "inputs": {},
192	      "outputs": {
193	        "result": { "source": "=js:$vars.accumulator" }
194	      }
195	    }
196	  ],
197	  "edges": [
198	    { "id": "e1", "sourceNodeId": "start", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "input" },
199	    { "id": "e2", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "bodyScript", "targetPort": "input" },
200	    { "id": "e3", "sourceNodeId": "bodyScript", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "loopBack" },
201	    { "id": "e4", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "end1", "targetPort": "input" }
202	  ],
203	  "variables": {
204	    "globals": [
205	      { "id": "inputItems", "direction": "in", "type": "array", "defaultValue": [] },
206	      { "id": "accumulator", "direction": "inout", "type": "number", "defaultValue": 0 },
207	      { "id": "result", "direction": "out", "type": "number" }
208	    ],
209	    "nodes": [
210	      { "id": "loop1.currentItem", "type": "any", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" } },
211	      { "id": "loop1.currentIndex", "type": "number", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" } },
212	      { "id": "loop1.collection", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" } },
213	      { "id": "loop1.output", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" } },
214	      { "id": "bodyScript.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "bodyScript", "outputId": "output" } },
215	      { "id": "bodyScript.error", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "bodyScript", "outputId": "error" } }
216	    ],
217	    "variableUpdates": {
218	      "bodyScript": [
219	        { "variableId": "accumulator", "expression": "=js:$vars.bodyScript.output" }
220	      ]
221	    }
222	  }
223	}
224	```
225	
226	Key points in this pattern:
227	- `bodyScript` has `"parentId": "loop1"` — places it inside the loop
228	- Script accesses `$vars.loop1.currentItem` for the current iteration value
229	- `variableUpdate` on `bodyScript` writes the script's return value back to `accumulator`
230	- `accumulator` is `inout` so it persists across iterations
231	- End node maps the final accumulated value to the `out` variable
232	
233	## Debug
234	
235	| Error | Cause | Fix |
236	| --- | --- | --- |
237	| Collection is empty or null | Expression evaluates to null/undefined | Check `collection` expression and upstream output |
238	| `$vars.loop1.currentItem` is undefined | Missing node variable binding or missing `parentId` | Add `loop1.currentItem` to `variables.nodes` and set `parentId` on body nodes |
239	| State variable not updating across iterations | Body node missing `parentId` | Add `"parentId": "<loopId>"` to every node inside the loop body |
240	| State variable becomes `NaN` | variableUpdate expression uses `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | Loop variables are not available in variableUpdate expressions. Do the computation in the script and reference `$vars.<bodyNodeId>.output` in the variableUpdate |
241	| Infinite loop | Edges wired incorrectly | Ensure only `loopBack` creates the cycle, not arbitrary edges |
242	| No output after loop | Missing `success` edge | Wire the `success` port to the next downstream node |
243
